Ana Paula, I heard you have two border collies. Did you know dog owners are part of my study?
My dogs? Really? What is the study about?
It is about dog owners and exercise. The study is done at the university, and the steps of every participant are measured with a small watch.
Interesting! And how are the participants chosen?
They are chosen from local vet clinics. Last year, ninety owners were invited, and sixty said yes.
And was anything published?
Yes. Our first finding was published in March. Dog owners walk about twenty minutes more every day.
That makes sense. My dogs are walked twice a day, in the rain or in the sun!

Good morning, and welcome to Health Minute on Coast Radio. A new study about sleep was published this week. The study was done in Jacksonville, and two hundred adults were chosen to take part. The participants were asked to do one simple thing: keep their phones out of the bedroom for one month. Their sleep was measured every night with a small watch. The finding is easy to remember. People who left the phone in the kitchen slept about thirty minutes more. The researchers say more evidence is needed, because the sample was small. But tonight, maybe your phone can sleep in the kitchen too.

Hi Ana Paula, this is Tom, from the university. Thank you for your interest in the dog study. Here is how it works. You are given one small watch for each dog. Your walks are measured for two weeks, and the information is collected automatically. Names are not used. Every participant is given a number, so your name is safe. At the end, the watches are collected at the vet clinic on Anastasia Boulevard. Last year, sixty owners were part of the study, and they all said it was easy. Call me back if you have questions. Bye!

A small study about sleep was planned at a clinic in Orlando. Forty adults were chosen from the clinic's patients. Each participant was given a sleep watch for two weeks. Their sleep was measured every night. The main finding was published in a health magazine.
